title: Senior Manager - Data Center Operations
text:
**About Us** 
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Visa will accept applications for this role until at least 12-03-2026

**Job Description**

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Data Center IT Operations is a first-line people leader responsible for the safe, reliable, and disciplined execution of Data Center IT Operations across enterprise data center environments. The role oversees teams supporting day-to-day data center operations, mainframe physical infrastructure activities, and storage and tape/media operations while ensuring work is completed to approved scope, service commitments, security requirements, and operational standards.

This position translates Director-level strategy and priorities into daily operating plans, clear accountability, effective staffing, measurable outcomes, and consistent execution. The role provides direct people leadership, operational governance, technical escalation, change and incident oversight, vendor coordination, audit readiness, and continuous improvement across the supported functions.

The Senior Manager is a working people leader. The role is expected to maintain sufficient technical depth to challenge plans, validate readiness, guide escalations, and make risk-based operating decisions, while relying on senior technical contributors and subject-matter experts for detailed engineering authority and platform-specific design decisions.

The Senior Manager collaborates with capacity planning, facilities, DCIM, engineering, finance, and business stakeholders by providing accurate operational data, site constraints, implementation demand, lifecycle information, and risk inputs needed for forecasting and investment decisions.

Proficiency

 

* Leadership Proficiency: Experienced first-line manager capable of leading 24x7 operational teams, senior technical contributors, and cross-functional delivery in a regulated, highly available environment.
* Technical Proficiency: Broad working knowledge across data center IT operations, hardware lifecycle execution, mainframe physical operations, enterprise storage, and tape/media handling, with the judgment to engage the correct engineering authority for specialized decisions.
* Operating Scope: Accountable for team performance, daily service execution, risk management, workforce readiness, controls, and stakeholder communication across assigned sites or operating functions.

Supported Organization and Role Alignment

The role is designed to provide direct people leadership and operational accountability for the following job families or equivalent roles, subject to the final organization design:

* **Data Center Operations Analysts and Senior Analysts:** 24x7 on-site operational coverage; change implementation; rack-and-stack; migration, turn-up, decommission, incident, remote-hands, inventory, documentation, and site-readiness activities.
* **Senior and Senior Consultant Data Center Engineers:** Advanced execution, small-project or process ownership, work-team guidance, technical escalation, documentation quality, operational improvement, and mentoring within the assigned job function.
* **Staff Data Center Engineers or Technical Leads:** Senior individual contributors providing change governance, complex escalation support, cross-site standards, process design, technical strategy input, and first-among-equals workload coordination without formal personnel-management authority.
* **Mainframe Operations Support Personnel:** Physical installation and lifecycle support, cabling and connectivity coordination, hardware change readiness, incident response, vendor activity, console or access coordination where applicable, documentation, and escalation to mainframe engineering teams.
* **Storage and Tape/Media Operations Personnel:** Physical storage infrastructure support, tape library and media operational activities, secure media handling and chain-of-custody controls, inventory reconciliation, vendor coordination, incident and change support, and escalation to storage or backup engineering teams.

Final direct-report assignments should be confirmed through the approved organization design. This profile establishes the management scope and accountabilities expected if these roles report to the Senior Manager.

Core Responsibilities

People Leadership and Workforce Management

* **Direct People Management:** Lead, coach, and develop direct reports through clear goals, regular feedback, performance management, development planning, recognition, and accountability.
* **Staffing and Coverage:** Maintain staffing and schedule coverage appropriate to business demand, including 24x7 operations where assigned. Manage timecards, attendance, leave coordination, required training, on-call participation, and escalation coverage in accordance with policy.
* **Talent and Succession:** Partner with recruiting and leadership to fill vacancies, onboard employees, build bench strength, identify successors, reduce single points of knowledge, and create development opportunities across operations, mainframe, and storage/tape disciplines.
* **Role Clarity:** Define decision rights, work expectations, handoffs, escalation paths, and ownership boundaries among people leaders, Staff engineers, Senior Consultants, Senior engineers, Analysts, vendors, and partner teams.
* **Team Culture:** Foster a culture of safety, service, inclusion, accountability, operational excellence, continuous learning, and respectful challenge.

Data Center IT Operations Management

* **Daily Operations:** Oversee day-to-day execution of changes, installations, rack-and-stack work, migrations, turn-ups, decommissions, break/fix activity, incident response, remote-hands requests, inventory support, and site-readiness work.
* **Work Prioritization:** Translate business priorities into executable daily and weekly plans. Balance urgency, customer impact, technical risk, available skills, approved change windows, service commitments, and staffing capacity.
* **Operational Handoffs:** Ensure shift turnover, open-work tracking, escalation notes, customer commitments, incident status, and incomplete activities are communicated accurately and acted upon.
* **Site Stewardship:** Maintain operational ownership for non-facilities data center areas within scope, including organization, housekeeping, staging, tools, test equipment, spares, consumables, labeling, access readiness, and visitor or vendor coordination.
* **Service Continuity:** Ensure the team can sustain critical operations during staffing shortages, severe weather, major incidents, business-continuity events, or other disruptions, using approved contingency and escalation procedures.

Mainframe, Storage, and Tape/Media Oversight

* **Mainframe Operations:** Provide people leadership and operational oversight for physical mainframe activities, including implementation readiness, installation and deinstallation support, connectivity and cabling coordination, incident support, vendor access, documentation, and escalation to platform engineering.
* **Storage Operations:** Oversee operational support for enterprise storage hardware and related physical infrastructure, including approved changes, hardware lifecycle events, break/fix coordination, cabling, inventory, documentation, and vendor engagement.
* **Tape and Media Operations:** Ensure tape library and removable-media activities follow approved procedures for handling, tracking, movement, storage, reconciliation, retention, destruction coordination, and chain of custody.
* **Technical Authority Boundaries:** Ensure platform design, configuration authority, architecture, and specialized engineering decisions remain with designated engineering owners. The Senior Manager is accountable for operational execution, readiness, controls, and escalation.
* **Lifecycle Coordination:** Coordinate lifecycle demand, maintenance windows, end-of-life risks, spares, vendor support, and implementation dependencies with Hardware Asset Management, engineering, procurement, security, and service owners.

**Change, Incident, Problem, and Escalation Governance**
--------------------------------------------------------

* **Change Governance:** Ensure assigned changes are reviewed for scope, approvals, implementation and backout plans, access, staffing, materials, dependencies, risk controls, customer communication, and validation evidence before execution.
* **Incident Leadership:** Lead or support operational response for high-severity or complex incidents, establishing clear ownership, timely escalation, evidence-based communication, recovery validation, and follow-through.
* **Problem Management:** Use recurring incidents, failed changes, defects, rework, control exceptions, and customer feedback to drive root-cause analysis, corrective actions, preventive controls, and sustained remediation.
* **Decision and Escalation:** Make timely decisions within delegated authority and escalate when business impact, safety, security, compliance, architecture, funding, or cross-organizational tradeoffs exceed the role’s authority.
* **After-Hours Leadership:** Participate in the established leadership escalation model and ensure appropriate technical and management support is available for critical events outside standard business hours.

Controls, Security, Safety, and Audit Readiness

* **Control Execution:** Ensure operational procedures support company policies, regulatory obligations, security requirements, change controls, asset controls, media controls, and documented evidence expectations.
* **Safety and Stop-Work:** Promote safe work practices and ensure employees or contractors pause and escalate work when unsafe conditions, unauthorized activity, inadequate controls, or material quality risks are identified.
* **Physical Security:** Enforce access, escort, visitor, vendor, material-movement, and restricted-area requirements. Escalate access anomalies and security concerns promptly.
* **Audit Readiness:** Maintain accurate records, evidence, inventories, reconciliations, procedures, training completion, corrective actions, and control-owner responses needed to support audits and risk reviews.
* **Media Governance:** Ensure secure media handling, inventory accuracy, chain of custody, retention and destruction coordination, exception management, and evidence quality for tape and other removable media within scope.

Operational Standards, Documentation, and Data Quality

* **Standardization:** Implement and reinforce consistent operating standards across shifts, sites, and supported platforms while allowing documented local variations where required.
* **Procedures and Runbooks:** Ensure SOPs, runbooks, checklists, escalation guides, implementation instructions, and training materials are current, usable, controlled, and understood by the team.
* **Systems of Record:** Ensure timely and accurate updates to approved ticketing, DCIM, CMDB, Hardware Asset Management, inventory, media, and operational reporting systems.
* **Data Quality:** Establish ownership for correcting discrepancies in asset records, rack elevations, device locations, cable records, inventory, media records, work notes, and completion evidence.
* **Knowledge Resilience:** Reduce dependence on individual subject-matter experts through cross-training, documented procedures, mentoring, simulations, and structured knowledge transfer.

Vendor, Partner, and Stakeholder Management

* **Vendor and Contractor Oversight:** Confirm scope, access, safety expectations, schedules, tools, materials, deliverables, evidence, and escalation paths for vendors, contractors, customer engineers, and service partners.
* **Cross-Functional Partnership:** Build effective working relationships with facilities, network, mainframe, storage, backup, security, Hardware Asset Management, DCIM, capacity planning, change management, incident management, procurement, finance, and business service owners.
* **Customer Communication:** Provide concise, risk-based communication on service status, delivery commitments, blockers, operational impacts, decisions, and corrective actions.
* **Leadership Representation:** Represent the operational perspective in planning forums, change reviews, incident calls, audit discussions, project reviews, and leadership meetings, escalating strategic or funding decisions to the Director.

**Metrics, Financial Stewardship, and Continuous Improvement**
--------------------------------------------------------------

* **Operational Measures:** Define and monitor measures such as change success, on-time completion, failed changes, rework, incident response, repeat incidents, backlog age, throughput, service-level attainment, inventory accuracy, media-control accuracy, documentation quality, audit findings, and corrective-action closure.
* **Performance Management:** Use data to identify trends, clarify accountability, prioritize improvements, and coach the team. Measures should support better decisions and sustained service improvement.
* **Continuous Improvement:** Lead initiatives that reduce manual effort, eliminate recurring failure modes, strengthen controls, improve workflow efficiency, and increase predictable service delivery.
* **Financial Stewardship:** Manage assigned operating expenses, tools, training, vendor usage, overtime, spares, and discretionary spending within delegated authority. Identify cost avoidance and efficiency opportunities without compromising safety, security, resilience, or control effectiveness.
* **Benefits Validation:** Set measurable outcomes for improvement initiatives and verify that adopted changes deliver the intended operational, risk, quality, or financial benefit.

Capacity Planning Collaboration, Not Ownership

* **Role Boundary:** The Senior Manager does not own enterprise capacity strategy, forecasting models, white-space planning, power and cooling forecasts, or capital capacity decisions.
* **Operational Inputs:** Provide accurate demand signals, rack and floor observations, deployment schedules, lifecycle events, backlog, staffing constraints, inventory needs, and implementation risks to the teams accountable for capacity planning.
* **Plan Review:** Participate in capacity reviews to validate operational feasibility, implementation sequencing, site readiness, resource requirements, and delivery risk.
* **Constraint Escalation:** Identify and escalate operational constraints involving space, power, cooling, cabling, access, staffing, tools, spares, or schedule conflicts to the accountable owner.

*This is an on-site position. An on-site position must be consistently performed at an assigned Visa office location and require daily commute to the office location*

**Qualifications**

Basic Qualifications:

 

* 8+ years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor's Degree or at least 5 years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g., Master's, MBA, JD, MD) or 2 years of work experience with a PhD, OR 11+ years of relevant work experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

 

* 9 or more years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor's Degree or 7 or more relevant years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g., Master's, MBA, JD, MD) or 3 or more years of experience with a PhD.
* 5+ years of direct people-leadership experience, including performance management, coaching, staffing, talent development, and accountability for operational outcomes.•
* Experience leading 24x7 data center operations teams and managing shift-based coverage models.
* Experience in financial services or another highly regulated, audit-intensive, high-availability environment.
* Experience with DCIM, CMDB, Hardware Asset Management, media-management, inventory, change-management, incident-management, ticketing, and workflow systems.
* + Experience supporting IBM Z or comparable mainframe physical operations, enterprise storage platforms, tape libraries, and secure removable-media processes.
* Experience establishing operational metrics, dashboards, control evidence, corrective-action programs, and data-driven improvement plans.
* Experience managing vendor performance, operational budgets, training investments, overtime, tools, spares, and service contracts.
* Relevant industry certifications in data center operations, IT service management, project management, infrastructure, security, storage, mainframe, or safety are beneficial.
* 10+ years of relevant experience in data center operations, infrastructure operations, mainframe operations, enterprise storage, backup/tape operations, hardware lifecycle management, or a related technology discipline.
* Experience leading teams in a production, highly available, regulated, or geographically distributed data center environment.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing change execution, incident response, problem management, vendor activity, operational controls, documentation, and service-level commitments.
* Broad working knowledge of data center physical infrastructure, including rack-and-stack practices, structured cabling, fiber and copper connectivity, labeling, power dependencies, equipment handling, inventory, and asset lifecycle processes.
* Working familiarity with mainframe physical environments, enterprise storage infrastructure, and tape/media operational controls, with the judgment to engage specialist engineering teams when required.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence across engineering, facilities, security, asset management, service management, vendors, and business stakeholders.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including concise executive escalation, risk communication, performance reporting, and operational decision documentation.
* Ability to participate in after-hours escalation support and work safely within a physical data center environment in accordance with applicable procedures.

**Information for US Applicants**

For roles located in the US, the estimated salary range for this position is $143,700.00 to $ 229,500.00 USD per year, which may include potential sales incentive payments (if applicable). Salary may vary depending on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location. In addition, this position may be eligible for bonus and equity.Visa has a comprehensive benefits package for which this position may be eligible that includes Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), FSA/HSA, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, and Wellness Program.

**Work Hours**

Varies upon the needs of the department.

**Travel Requirements**

This position requires travel 5-10% of the time.

**Mental/Physical Requirements**

This position will be performed in an office setting. The position will require the incumbent to sit and stand at a desk, communicate in person and by telephone, frequently operate standard office equipment, such as telephones and computers.

**Visa is an EEO Employer**

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protect veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.
